newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo PGM futures surge on S.Africa mine strike.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo PGM futures surge on S.Africa mine strike.

text.p: Tokyo platinum and palladium futures closed sharply higher on Wednesday, as news of an illegal strike at the Rustenburg platinum mine in South Africa triggered active buying, traders said.
The June, August and October palladium futures contracts surged by the daily 22 yen per gram limit by the close.
South Africa's Anglo American Platinum Corp Ltd said on Wednesday that it had had an illegal work stoppage at the Amandelbult section of its Rustenburg mine.
Rustenburg has a current production capacity of 1.3 million ounces of platinum a year.
The benchmark April 1998 of yen-based palladium futures ended 18 yen higher at 589 yen per gram.
Platinum futures ended higher across the board. Prices ranged from 19 to 36 yen higher, with benchmark April rising 32 yen to close at 1,398 yen per gram.
Traders said there had been market talk since last week that the Rustenburg mine would go on strike.

"I'd like to watch how the strike helps tighten global supplies," a trade house official said. Individual investors hold a large amount of shorts in palladium futures, and their short-covering was also behind today's rally, traders said.
Activity in gold futures was slow compared to the volatile platinum and palladium market.
Gold futures ranged from four to nine yen higher, with benchmark April 1998 closing four yen up at 1,282 yen per gram.
Bullion was quoted at $344.60/344.90 per ounce at 0750 GMT, against late Tuesday Asian levels of $342.70/343.00.
"Investors are shifting their money to PGM contracts away from the gold market," a brokerage house trader said.
Benchmark April silver closed 1.7 yen per 10 grams higher at 180.9 yen.
